title: skills: the ask-data skill's zero-match row reads the `candidates` list once list_datasets fills it
body:
epic:#34659#1 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjMnXJdSZifpEN5i7aU

Filing gate: ④ a child of the cross-lane parent #34659 (the 「MCP 二期与问数」 epic). The maintainer set who files this epic's cards, in this session's chat, 2026-11-17, verbatim: 「你应该负责立卡，对方只是派发处理」. The gap was reported to this session by the dispatching seat `repo:objectstack#3` on #34659 (comment 6947907343, repeated in 6948819963); the filer did not re-read the code behind it. It is the `Skills-docs` follow-up PR #34828 names.

## Why

The published ask-data skill tells a client, on a zero-match, to read the whole catalogue and judge near readings itself. Once the server returns `candidates`, that wording teaches the slower and less reliable path.

## Evidence

- #34685 / PR #34792 wrote the zero-match row before the F1 ruling's server change existed.
- #34761 adds `candidates` to the output shape; #34763 fills it.

## Scope

- In `skills/objectstack-ask/SKILL.md`: on a zero-match, read `candidates`; when any is listed, ask which is meant, name each candidate's label, dataset and description, and compute nothing; never treat a candidate as a match. With none listed, fall back and say so.
- The served `/mcp/skill` text says the same (single source, #34686).
- Its eval cases cover: candidates listed, none listed.

## Done when

- The skill, the served text and the tool description of #34763 state one rule in the same words.

## Relations

- Parent: #34659. Ruling: #34691 F1 = B.
- Blocked-by: #34763
- Governed surface: `skills/**`.
